pages.title: Ranges
pages.content:
Two kinds of shelf: paint and paper. House Matt €58 (2.5 L), Wood & Metal Eggshell €34 (1 L), Lime Wash €46 (2.5 L), Sample Pot €6 (100 ml), Linen-Weave Wallpaper €72 (roll 10.05 × 0.52 m) and Grasscloth Wallpaper €138 (roll 5.5 × 0.91 m).

Mixed paint is ready to collect in 2 hours. Delivery in Rotterdam €9, free over €150.

pages.title: Colour Mixing
pages.content:
Bring the room in, we mix it to match. A phone photo of the wall, a chip, a fabric or a flake of old paint is enough. Lena reads the colour, writes a recipe and mixes a 100 ml sample pot. A drawdown card dries for 20 minutes and is checked by the window, not under the shop lights. Then the order is mixed and the recipe number goes on the lid.

Colour match at the counter is free. In-home colour match visit €45, deducted from orders over €200.

pages.title: Wallpaper
pages.content: Paper is ordered by the roll and the batch. Tomás calculates the rolls from your room; order every roll from one batch, plus one spare. Wallpaper not in stock is ordered in 3–5 working days.

pages.title: Order & Collection
pages.content: Mixed paint is ready to collect in 2 hours, free. Orders placed before 15:00 Tuesday to Saturday are delivered in Rotterdam the next working day: €9, free over €150. Unopened stock may be returned within 14 days; mixed paint is not returnable.

pages.title: About
pages.content:
Ines Valk founded Toso Paints in 2009 after years as a decorator in Rotterdam, with one mixing counter, a tinting machine and a simple conviction: a colour is chosen against the room, not the chip.

A day at the shop follows a quiet routine. Lena opens the tinting machine at 09:00, Yusuf prepares the day's deliveries, Amara leaves for in-home visits, and drawdown cards dry on the rack by the window until they are checked in daylight.

pages.title: Newsletter
pages.content: Once a month we send one colour note: a room, a recipe and what we learned at the swatch table. Write to hello@tosopaints.example to join.

pages.title: Visit
pages.content:
Toso Paints, Verfstraat 18, 3011 Rotterdam, Netherlands. Tue–Fri 09:00–18:00, Sat 09:00–17:00 (swatch table 10:00–13:00), Sun and Mon closed.

Take tram 8 to Verfstraat; the shop is a two-minute walk from the stop. Email hello@tosopaints.example or call +31 10 000 1809.

posts.title: What happens at the Saturday swatch table
posts.excerpt: Hands-on testing, comparing undertones, and seeing how wet emulsion shifts as it dries.
posts.content:
Every Saturday between 10:00 and 13:00 Mei sets up a long table by the window with sample boards, brushes and a pot of every finish we mix. Visitors paint a board, set it against the wall photo on their phone and watch it dry.

Wet paint always reads darker and cooler than dry paint. The table is there so that you see the change before you buy a tin. Pieter de Wit runs a short brushwork demonstration on the first Saturday of the month.

posts.title: Why we sell a sample pot before a tin
posts.excerpt: Testing 100 ml on your own wall prevents costly mistakes under real room light.
posts.content:
A sample pot is 100 ml of any colour, mixed to order, for €6. It is enough for a card or a square metre of wall.

Lena writes the recipe for the pot and keeps it on file, so if the colour works the tin is mixed from the same recipe. If it does not, the sample cost you less than a tin of the wrong green.

posts.title: One green, two rooms: north light and south light
posts.excerpt: How exposure and shadow change the perception of a single moss recipe.
posts.content:
The same recipe went onto a north-facing kitchen in Kralingen and a south-facing living room in Noord. In the kitchen it read grey and cool; in the living room it read warm and almost yellow.

Amara matched the kitchen one step warmer after the drawdown check. The lesson is the one the shop is built on: a colour is chosen against the room, not the chip.

posts.title: Hanging the first drop straight
posts.excerpt: Why the first strip decides the whole wall.
posts.content:
Tomás starts every wall with a plumb line, not the corner. Corners are rarely straight, and a paper hung from the corner drifts.

Paste the wall, hang the first drop to the line, smooth from the centre out with a wide brush and check the seam against the second drop before the paste sets. Order every roll from one batch, plus one spare.

posts.title: Drawdown cards, and why we wait twenty minutes
posts.excerpt: A card dries for 20 minutes and is checked by the window, not under the shop lights.
posts.content:
A drawdown card is a stiff card painted with an even film of the mixed colour. It dries for 20 minutes, because most paint shifts in the first quarter of an hour.

We then carry it to the window and hold it against the wall photo. If it is off, Lena adjusts the recipe by a drop at a time and we paint a second card.

posts.title: Eggshell on old skirting
posts.excerpt: Preparing old woodwork for a low-sheen finish.
posts.content:
Wood & Metal Eggshell is a low-sheen finish for skirting, doors and radiators, sold in 1 L for €34. On old gloss, sand lightly, wipe, and prime any bare patches.

Two thin coats beat one thick coat. Leave it overnight before it meets a vacuum cleaner.
